Consult Summary:
- Telehealth consult for 4-weeks postpartum woman with acute onset shortness of breath at rest; advised urgent hospital evaluation for possible pulmonary embolism.

History:
- Presenting complaint: New shortness of breath starting about 1 hour prior while sitting and watching TV.
- Associated symptoms: Nonproductive cough since yesterday; palpitations/feeling heart racing; no chest pain; chest soreness with deep inspiration; C-section scar tenderness. No prior similar episodes reported.
- Pertinent negatives: No chest pain; infant well with no cough/cold symptoms.
- Past medical history: Cesarean section 4 weeks ago.
- Medications: Codeine used regularly post-op; not taken for 1 week (dose/route/frequency not documented). No other medications reported.
- Allergies: Ibuprofen (reaction not described).
- Family history: Mother had leg clots (DVT) per patient.
- Social history: At home with newborn; partner at work. No other social history or preventive care discussed.

Examination:
- Vitals: Not obtained.
- Examination findings: Remote pulse check—patient counted 30 beats during a brief timed interval; clinician interpreted heart rate as slightly fast. No in-person exam performed.

Impression:
- Acute dyspnea at rest in a postpartum patient (4 weeks post–C-section) with cough and palpitations; concern for venous thromboembolism/pulmonary embolism. Differential includes anxiety or viral respiratory illness, but PE prioritized given postpartum status.

Plan:
- Immediate evaluation in hospital/ED recommended for possible PE/DVT.
- Transport options discussed: ambulance vs self-transport; patient chose self-transport with baby and was advised to go promptly and bring baby supplies.
- Medication advice: Do not take codeine for now.
- Education: Discussed postpartum clot risk and that hospital can provide treatment to reduce clot if confirmed.
- Follow-up: Not specified in transcript.

Quality checks (always include at bottom of note, or fill document_quality):
- Missing expected elements: Full review of systems (fever, leg pain/swelling, hemoptysis, syncope), vital signs, full medication reconciliation (including doses/routes/frequencies), breastfeeding status, smoking status, surgical/obstetric details (intra/post-op course), VTE risk factors (immobility, travel, thrombophilia), and safety-net/red flag instructions beyond “go to hospital.”
- Internal conflicts: Date of birth—patient stated 04/20/1980; clinician later said 1983 (conflict noted).
- Transcript quality: Generally clear; some pauses and incomplete statements; no major audio issues reported.
